title: Enterprise GPU Pool Sizing & Failure-Mode Playbook (questionnaire + recommender)
creator: Daniel Kim
description:
Purpose: produce a prescriptive playbook and intake questionnaire to recommend GPU pool class, reserved throughput target, and automated scaling + escalation behavior for enterprise reserved pools. Scope: customer-facing questionnaire + backend recommender rules + failure-mode matrix (preemption, cold-starts, cross-tenant noisy neighbor), sample defaults for 3 tiers (pilot, production, mission-critical). Excludes billing contract language and legal terms (handled by Revenue/Legal).

Background: We frequently onboard enterprise customers asking for ‘X tokens/min’ or ‘Y concurrent users’ without a consistent conversion to GPU tier, burst policy, or SLO. Sales and Solutions currently rely on ad-hoc spreadsheets and engineering estimates which increases onboarding time and leads to overprovisioning. Goal is to reduce time-to-provision, improve first-week SLO compliance, and provide a deterministic fallback matrix for when usage spikes or GPUs are preempted.
acceptance_criteria: Customer questionnaire (Google Form + one-page PDF) that maps usage signals (tokens/min, avg seq length, expected p95 latency) to recommended GPU families and pool sizes
Backend ruleset (human-readable) that can be implemented by ENG: mapping inputs -> {GPU class, baseline_reserved_units, burst_policy, cooldowns, fallback_model_variant}
Failure-mode matrix covering at least 5 scenarios with operator runbooks and automated escalation steps
Pilot runbook template and checklist for 2 pilot customers with measurable SLOs and cost delta tracking
Sign-off from Solutions, Infra Eng (serving runtime), and Legal for the questionnaire and default recommendations
decisions: Use three sizing tiers (Pilot, Production, Mission) rather than continuous sizing to simplify sales conversations
Default GPU families: Pilot -> L4, Production -> A10/A100 (mixed), Mission -> H100 (or equivalent) with explicit quantization recommendation
Reserved throughput expressed as tokens-per-minute and concurrent-exec units to align with billing and runtime capacity signals
Include a ‘graceful degradation’ route: on preemption or capacity shortage, automatically route to a smaller model variant with a documented quality delta
next_steps: Finalize questionnaire draft and distribute to Solutions for 1st feedback (owner: Priya)
Workshop with Serving Runtime (owner: Mateo Alvarez) to translate rules into implementable capacity signals (2/02)
Create the failure-mode matrix and attach runbook snippets for PagerDuty escalation (owner: Maya Chen)
Prepare pilot onboarding with customer A and customer B (weeks of 2/15 and 3/01) and track SLOs for 30 days
